title: Worked Examples: Balancing Equations & Reaction Classification
objectives: Identify oxidising and reducing agents in redox reactions
Predict precipitation reactions and deduce spectator ions

blocks.heading: Redox Analysis Strategy
blocks.content:
In any redox reaction:
• Substance oxidised = gains oxygen or loses hydrogen.
• Substance reduced = loses oxygen or gains hydrogen.
• Oxidising agent = causes oxidation (is itself reduced).
• Reducing agent = causes reduction (is itself oxidised).

workedExamples.prompt: Identify the substances oxidised, reduced, oxidising agent, and reducing agent in: CuO + H2 -> Cu + H2O
steps: Step 1: CuO loses oxygen to become Cu. Loss of oxygen = REDUCTION. Hence CuO is reduced.
Step 2: H2 gains oxygen to become H2O. Gain of oxygen = OXIDATION. Hence H2 is oxidised.
Step 3: The substance that gets reduced (CuO) is the OXIDISING AGENT.
Step 4: The substance that gets oxidised (H2) is the REDUCING AGENT.
workedExamples.answer: Oxidised: H2; Reduced: CuO; Oxidising Agent: CuO; Reducing Agent: H2

workedExamples.prompt: What happens when an aqueous solution of sodium sulphate (Na2SO4) is mixed with barium chloride (BaCl2)?
steps: Step 1: Write ions present: Na+, SO4(2-), Ba(2+), Cl-.
Step 2: Exchange ions: Ba(2+) pairs with SO4(2-) to form BaSO4.
Step 3: Na+ pairs with Cl- to form NaCl.
Step 4: BaSO4 is insoluble in water and forms a white precipitate.
Step 5: Balanced equation: Na2SO4(aq) + BaCl2(aq) -> BaSO4(s) + 2NaCl(aq).
workedExamples.answer: White precipitate of BaSO4 is formed (Double displacement reaction)

practice.prompt: In the reaction: MnO2 + 4HCl -> MnCl2 + 2H2O + Cl2, which substance is oxidised?
hints: HCl loses hydrogen to become Cl2. Loss of hydrogen is oxidation.
practice.feedback: HCl is oxidised to Cl2 (loss of hydrogen), while MnO2 is reduced to MnCl2 (loss of oxygen).

takeaways: Oxidation and reduction always occur simultaneously (redox).
Barium sulphate (BaSO4) is the classic white precipitate in CBSE lab exams.
